page: Microsoft Azure E20as_v6 is an Eav6-family virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this server features 20 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 10 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is configured with 160.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance utilizes the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and contains no local storage, though it is Premium Storage capable. There are no onboard GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance for both stress-ng and Geekbench falls in the middle 50% average tier. Memory bandwidth tests, including read-only small block (1520.39 GB/sec) and uncached large block read/write (76.12 GB/sec and 57.09 GB/sec respectively), also register in the average tier. Text processing is a relative strength, scoring in the top 25% on Geekbench. For language model workloads, the server achieves strong results for text generation with small 135M models (327.86 tokens/sec), but exhibits weak performance for large 70B model prompt processing (5.46 tokens/sec).

From a resource density perspective, the E20as_v6 offers high memory capacity relative to its compute footprint, making it a memory-optimized option. The lack of local storage requires reliance on external Premium Storage, which represents a key architectural tradeoff. Given the average multi-core and database benchmark results, alongside the high memory-to-vCPU ratio, this server is suited for memory-intensive workloads such as relational databases, caching layers like Redis, and moderate-scale data processing tasks that fit within its 160.0 GB memory envelope.
